exclusion_criteria: Generic agent or chatbot papers not focused on scientific research workflows.
Tools limited to summarization, reference formatting, citation recommendation, or manuscript polishing without claim-evidence verification or provenance.
Wet-lab robotics or laboratory automation papers with no literature-review, manuscript-generation, or claim-grounding component.
Papers focused only on plagiarism detection, bibliometrics, or reference-style compliance.
Non-scholarly commentary, tutorials, news, patents, or non-English records.
inclusion_criteria: English-language scholarly records indexed by Crossref or Semantic Scholar.
Works on AI/LLM systems that automate at least two of the following: literature search/review, experiment design or execution, result analysis, manuscript drafting.
Papers on citation verification, claim grounding, evidence attribution, provenance tracking, or novelty/prior-art evaluation in scientific research workflows.
Benchmark, audit, or critical-analysis papers that evaluate hallucination, unsupported citations or conclusions, provenance quality, or reproducibility for scientific assistants or agents.
Priority to computational, simulated, or otherwise explicitly traceable experiment settings where generated claims can be linked to recorded evidence.
key_concepts: scientific claim verification and evidence attribution
hallucination, unsupported conclusions, and reproducibility benchmarks
queries: autonomous scientific research agents literature review experiment execution paper writing
scientific discovery llm agents end-to-end research workflow evidence provenance citation verification
retrieval-augmented scientific writing citation grounding claim verification scholarly sources
scientific claim verification evidence attribution provenance research papers large language models
novelty evaluation prior art search scientific research agents literature-based discovery
benchmark autonomous research agents hallucination unsupported conclusions reproducibility scientific discovery
review_question: What scholarly systems and evaluations address end-to-end autonomous scientific research agents that connect literature claims, experiment evidence, and novelty assessment, and how do they benchmark citation verification, evidence provenance, hallucination, and unsupported conclusions against baseline methods?
scope_limitations: This bounded metadata search is intended to support one credible first study, not an exhaustive systematic review.
Query wording emphasizes AI/LLM-driven scientific workflow automation and may miss relevant work described with different domain-specific terminology.
Absence from retrieved results is not proof of novelty or nonexistence; follow-up full-text screening, citation snowballing, and domain expansion would still be needed.
